entrances.note: In by the street door, at left, from Main Street.
In by the street door, at left, from Main Street.

LOOK_AT.say: A bell for summoning the clerk.
repeat: A card beside it reads RING FOR SERVICE, in the same hand as the card that reads NO CREDIT.
I've looked at this bell three times now. A lesser man would have rung it. So would a braver one.
then: The handle is worn to bare brass, which tells you how often the clerk is elsewhere.

repeat: Nothing. It is waiting me out.
Still nothing. The bell and I have reached an understanding, and the understanding is silence.

overrides.USE: I rang it. The clerk arrived from a direction the building does not have.

LOOK_AT.say: I won't be examining the spittoon closely. Some economies are false.
repeat: Brass, and emptied. In a hotel lobby this counts as gentility.
It has been moved twice since this morning and it is still in the wrong place.
There is a ring on the carpet where it used to be and a ring where it is.
Nothing, mercifully.
Nothing.
Nothing. We have both been spared.

overrides.PICK_UP: Not for five dollars. Not for a room. Not for anything this hotel has ever offered.

LOOK_AT.say: My line is ruled through, respectfully. The clerk did it with a straightedge. In this town even the erasures are filed.

repeat: Forty-one names. I've read all of them, and I don't know one.
Mine is the last, and it's spelled in a way I haven't previously encountered.
then: 'Thaddeus Grubbe.' The hotel has added exactly the letter it felt I was missing.

LISTEN_TO.say: Pages settling. Mine has already been turned.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing.
Nothing. It is a list of people who are elsewhere.

overrides.PICK_UP: It is the register. It stays on the desk and the desk stays where it is.
overrides.USE: I corrected my name in it. The next morning it was wrong again, differently. The register is alive, or the clerk is loyal to some principle I lack.

LOOK_AT.say: The Bay of Naples, carried four hundred miles on purpose. Somebody here believed in something real once. I've started to respect that.
An engraving of the Bay of Naples, in a hotel lobby, in a mining camp, four hundred miles from a paved road. Somebody carried this here on purpose.
repeat: The Bay of Naples, in a mining camp, four hundred miles from a paved road.
It is hung too high, which suggests it was hung by somebody who did not want it looked at closely.
Nothing.
Nothing. It is a long way from home and so am I, and only one of us is framed.

overrides.PICK_UP: It is hung too high for a man who has not been invited to touch it.

repeat: There is a goat on the nearest peak, looking out of the picture as though it was promised a better frame.
The signature is larger than the mountain. That, at least, is an honest account of the painter's priorities.
then: It is not one of our mountains; the painter never came west of the frame shop.

LISTEN_TO.say: Canvas, ticking in a draft. The draft is real, at least.
repeat: The frame creaks. It is the most western thing about it.
Nothing. A painting of a mountain is quieter than a mountain, and that is the only improvement on offer.

overrides.PULL: Behind it: wall. I don't know what I expected. More wall, perhaps, but honest about it.

LOOK_AT.say: The lobby clock, nineteen minutes off the Registrar's. After what I've learned, a lie that small is practically good manners.
A lobby clock. It disagrees with the Registrar's clock by nineteen minutes and neither has ever been challenged.
repeat: Nineteen minutes off the Registrar's, and neither has ever been challenged.
It is slow. In this town that is nearly an act of kindness.

LISTEN_TO.say: Ticking. Slightly slow. I'm not going to say anything.
repeat: Ticking. Slow.
Ticking. I'm still not going to say anything.

LOOK_AT.say: Forty keys. Mine's still out. The clerk hasn't asked for it back, which is either tact or a backlog.
Forty keys. Four of them are out.
repeat: Four out of forty. The four are not near each other.
Number nineteen is mine! I've looked at it more than a man should look at a key.
then: The hotel is one-tenth occupied and charges as though it were not.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. A key only speaks when dropped.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing.
Brass on wood, faintly, when the door goes.

PICK_UP.say: Number three. Mine, by arrangement with a piano. The clerk watched it leave the rack as if it might not come back, which shows how little he knows of my alternatives.
PICK_UP.sceneLine: docs/121-the-not-done-list.md::### N-3 and N-4 · The objects: the lines · **THE KEY RACK** · *the hotel lobby, once he has a room* - PICK UP, *the first time*

PICK_UP.say: The other two belong to men I have never seen. I shall leave them their mystery.
PICK_UP.sceneLine: docs/121-the-not-done-list.md::### N-3 and N-4 · The objects: the lines · **THE KEY RACK** · *the hotel lobby, once he has a room* - PICK UP, *again*

overrides.PICK_UP: Three keys, and mine is one, and the other two belong to men I've never seen. The hotel is fuller of mystery than of guests.

LOOK_AT.say: A settee in a color that was once a decision.
repeat: A settee in worn blue plush, gone shiny at both arms and nowhere in the middle.
Two men have sat at either end of this for years and neither has moved to the center.
It's the only comfortable thing I've seen since the coach, and the coach wasn't comfortable.
then: Someone has slept on it recently, and at length.

LISTEN_TO.say: Horsehair, sighing, same as when I was alive.
Horsehair, resettling. It sighs longer than furniture should.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing. Nobody is sitting on it and nobody is going to.

overrides.USE: I've sat on it. That's what happened next.

LOOK_AT.say: An upright piano in the corner of the lobby, under a fern that is doing better than it is. The hotel calls this corner the parlor.
repeat: Walnut, with a brass plate: DONATED BY THE CONSOLATION IMPROVEMENT COMPANY. There is no plate saying who has played it since.
The clerk dusts it every morning, around the keys. He does not touch the keys. Neither does anyone else.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing, until a cart goes by.
repeat: Still wrong. The A is the worst. The A is always the worst.
Four minutes' work, and a room for the night. I've done the arithmetic, which I gather is frowned on here.
then: Then every string answers, and every one of them is wrong in its own direction.

LOOK_AT.say: Main Street through glass with a wave in it.
repeat: A man outside has been about to cross the street for the whole of my stay. The glass makes him reconsider in waves.
My own reflection, rippling. Even the window hasn't decided whether I've arrived.
then: The town ripples, like it has not set yet.

LISTEN_TO.say: The street, muffled. The glass keeps out the words and lets the arguing through.
repeat: A wagon, a dog, a man insisting. The glass lets the insisting through.
Somebody laughing on the boardwalk. Through the window it sounds like an opinion.

overrides.OPEN: Painted shut. The street gets in anyway, one draft at a time.

LOOK_AT.say: A parlor stove with a nickel rail, polished.
repeat: Unlit. It has been unlit since I arrived, in a lobby with a rail for drying gloves.
The rail is for drying gloves. Nobody in Consolation owns gloves.
then: It is the only thing in this building anyone has spent an afternoon on.

repeat: Nothing.
Nothing at all.

overrides.OPEN: Cold, and empty, and it has been both for some time.

hotspots.name: THE STAIRS

LOOK_AT.say: Worn in the middle by men going up hopeful and coming down otherwise.
repeat: Stairs to the rooms, carpeted for the first four treads and bare above that. The carpet ran out.
Somebody measured wrong, or somebody ran out of money on the fifth tread.
The bare treads are worn more than the carpeted ones. Everyone is going up.

LISTEN_TO.say: The fourth step confesses under any weight at all.
repeat: Somebody on the landing, not moving. There is always somebody on the landing not moving.
Still there.
Boards. Two rooms, both occupied, neither talking.

WALK_TO.say: The stairs come with a room, sir. They are not sold separately.

USE.say: The stairs come with a room, sir. They are not sold separately.

OPEN.say: The stairs come with a room, sir. They are not sold separately.

exits.name: THE STREET DOOR

LOOK_AT.say: The door out onto Main Street, with a bell that does not work and a mat that has given up.
repeat: The bell is a formality. Everybody who comes in is already known.
The street, past it. It is always brighter than I remember.

LISTEN_TO.say: The street. Boots on the boardwalk.
repeat: Boots. Two men, and neither of them is coming in.
Nothing. It has gone quiet out there, which happens about four.
